"# ECHOES OF THE FALLEN
## A Detailed 2D Open-World Action RPG

Create a complete, highly polished, fully playable 2D action RPG titled \"ECHOES OF THE FALLEN\".

This must be a genuine 2D action RPG with detailed pixel art, real-time combat, exploration, character progression, quests, loot and a large interconnected world.

IMPORTANT: The game must prioritize gameplay depth, beautiful environments, smooth controls and satisfying combat.

Do NOT create a simple platformer, turn-based RPG, idle game or basic top-down walking simulator.

==================================================
1. GAME CONCEPT AND STORY
==================================================

The game takes place in a mysterious fantasy world called AETHERIA.

Long ago, the world was protected by ancient magical structures known as the Echo Monuments.

After a mysterious catastrophe, these structures became corrupted and strange creatures began appearing throughout the world.

Ancient settlements disappeared, forests became dangerous and forgotten civilizations were buried beneath the ruins.

The player controls a young wanderer who discovers an unusual connection to the ancient Echo Monuments.

Explore the world, discover forgotten civilizations, meet interesting characters, uncover hidden locations and gradually discover the truth behind the catastrophe.

Tell the story through exploration, dialogue, environmental storytelling and optional discoveries.

Avoid excessive cinematic cutscenes.

==================================================
2. ART STYLE AND GRAPHICS
==================================================

Create exceptionally detailed 2D pixel art.

Visual inspiration:
- Hyper Light Drifter.
- CrossCode.
- Eastward.
- Modern high-quality pixel-art RPGs.

The game must have:
- Detailed environmental tiles.
- Beautiful character sprites.
- Smooth character animations.
- Animated vegetation.
- Water reflections and movement.
- Atmospheric lighting.
- Animated environmental particles.
- Beautiful spell effects.
- Detailed buildings and architecture.
- Distinctive enemy designs.

Use carefully designed pixel-art palettes.

Avoid generic flat-colored environments.

Make every region visually recognizable.

The world should feel handcrafted rather than randomly assembled.

==================================================
3. CAMERA AND WORLD VIEW
==================================================

Use a top-down camera with a slightly elevated perspective.

IMPORTANT:
The camera must show a relatively LARGE area around the player.

Use a wider camera view than typical zoomed-in RPG games.

The player should remain clearly visible while the camera shows surrounding terrain, enemies, paths and environmental details.

Implement smooth camera following.

Allow adjustable camera zoom in the settings.

Provide:
- Normal zoom.
- Wide zoom.
- Close zoom.

Default to a relatively wide view.

Do not make the world feel cramped.

==================================================
4. WORLD DESIGN
==================================================

Create a large interconnected fantasy world divided into distinct regions.

Initially implement these areas:

A. GREENFALL FOREST
- Dense forests.
- Ancient trees.
- Hidden paths.
- Small settlements.
- Abandoned shrines.
- Forest creatures.

B. THE FORGOTTEN KINGDOM
- Ruined castles.
- Old streets.
- Abandoned buildings.
- Ancient libraries.
- Hidden treasure rooms.

C. FROSTBOUND MOUNTAINS
- Snow-covered terrain.
- Frozen caves.
- Mountain paths.
- Ancient monuments.

D. THE SUNKEN DEPTHS
- Underground caverns.
- Glowing crystals.
- Ancient underground structures.
- Dangerous creatures.

E. THE CENTRAL SANCTUARY
- A peaceful settlement.
- Merchants.
- NPCs.
- Upgrade stations.
- Quest givers.
- A central hub for the player.

Make regions interconnected through paths, caves, gates and shortcuts.

Some locations should require progression or special abilities to access.

Use a consistent world map.

==================================================
5. PLAYER CHARACTER
==================================================

Create a detailed animated pixel-art protagonist.

The player should have:
- Idle animation.
- Walking animation.
- Running animation.
- Dodge animation.
- Attack animation.
- Casting animation.
- Damage animation.

Allow the player to customize:
- Outfit colors.
- Cosmetic accessories.
- Appearance details.

Make the protagonist visually recognizable.

==================================================
6. REAL-TIME COMBAT
==================================================

Combat is one of the most important aspects of this game.

It must feel responsive, fluid and satisfying.

Implement:
- Fast basic attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Combos.
- Dodging.
- Blocking or defensive abilities.
- Magical abilities.
- Area-of-effect attacks.
- Cooldowns.
- Stamina or energy management.

Create several distinct magical abilities:

1. ARCANE BURST
A fast magical projectile.

2. BLINK
A short-distance movement ability that avoids incoming attacks.

3. NOVA
An area attack surrounding the player.

4. FROST BIND
Temporarily slows nearby enemies.

5. ECHO STRIKE
A powerful ability that releases stored magical energy.

Allow abilities to be unlocked and upgraded.

Make combat skill-based rather than button-mashing.

Use clear visual feedback for hits, dodges, enemy attacks and ability activation.

==================================================
7. ENEMIES AND BOSSES
==================================================

Create diverse enemy types.

Examples:
- Small forest creatures.
- Fast aggressive enemies.
- Armored guardians.
- Ranged magical creatures.
- Large elite monsters.
- Ancient corrupted guardians.

Each enemy should have distinct behavior.

Implement:
- Patrol.
- Detection.
- Chasing.
- Attacking.
- Dodging or repositioning.
- Taking damage.
- Defeat animations.

Create several boss encounters.

Bosses should have:
- Unique visual designs.
- Multiple attack patterns.
- Different combat phases.
- Clearly telegraphed attacks.
- Distinctive arenas.
- Rewarding victory sequences.

Boss fights should require learning attack patterns.

==================================================
8. RPG PROGRESSION
==================================================

Create a meaningful character progression system.

Include:
- Character level.
- Experience points.
- Health.
- Energy.
- Stamina.
- Attack power.
- Defense.
- Movement speed.

Enemies and quests reward experience.

Leveling up grants progression points.

Create a skill tree with three branches:

ARCANE:
Focus on magical damage and elemental abilities.

MOBILITY:
Focus on movement, dodging and speed.

GUARDIAN:
Focus on defense, survivability and counterattacks.

Allow players to choose their preferred playstyle.

==================================================
9. LOOT AND EQUIPMENT
==================================================

Create a rewarding loot system.

Item rarities:

- Common.
- Uncommon.
- Rare.
- Epic.
- Legendary.

Add collectible:
- Magical crystals.
- Ancient relics.
- Crafting materials.
- Healing supplies.
- Upgrade components.
- Cosmetic items.

Equipment should have meaningful statistics and visual differences.

Allow the player to inspect, compare and equip discovered items.

Add an inventory with limited space.

Include equipment management and item sorting.

==================================================
10. QUESTS AND NPCS
==================================================

Create a variety of quests.

Main quests:
- Discover ancient monuments.
- Investigate corrupted regions.
- Find missing explorers.
- Recover forgotten artifacts.

Side quests:
- Help villagers.
- Find lost objects.
- Explore hidden locations.
- Defeat dangerous creatures.
- Discover secret areas.

NPCs should have individual dialogue and useful information.

Create a simple quest journal.

Clearly display current objectives.

Avoid repetitive fetch quests as the only form of content.

==================================================
11. EXPLORATION AND SECRETS
==================================================

Exploration should be rewarding.

Add:
- Hidden caves.
- Secret rooms.
- Treasure chests.
- Optional boss encounters.
- Ancient puzzles.
- Hidden shortcuts.
- Rare collectible objects.
- Environmental storytelling.

Allow the player to discover things naturally without constantly following quest markers.

Create a minimap and a larger world map.

Show discovered and undiscovered areas differently.

==================================================
12. MOBILE AND DESKTOP CONTROLS
==================================================

Desktop:
- WASD or arrow keys: movement.
- Mouse or keyboard: combat abilities.
- Space: dodge.
- E: interaction.
- I: inventory.
- M: map.
- Escape: pause.

Mobile:
- Left virtual joystick.
- Dedicated attack button.
- Dodge button.
- Three or four ability buttons.
- Interaction button.
- Inventory and map buttons.

Make all mobile controls responsive.

Allow adjustable button sizes and positions if practical.

Support landscape mobile orientation.

Do not let the interface obstruct the gameplay.

==================================================
13. USER INTERFACE
==================================================

Create a beautiful fantasy RPG interface.

During gameplay display:
- Health bar.
- Energy bar.
- Experience bar.
- Character level.
- Current objective.
- Ability cooldowns.
- Minimap.

Create separate interfaces for:
- Main menu.
- Inventory.
- Character stats.
- Skill tree.
- Quest journal.
- World map.
- Equipment.
- Settings.

Use a consistent visual design.

Make menus readable and attractive.

==================================================
14. AUDIO AND ATMOSPHERE
==================================================

Include atmospheric music and sound effects if possible.

Examples:
- Forest ambience.
- Wind.
- Water.
- Footsteps.
- Combat sounds.
- Magical effects.
- Enemy sounds.
- Environmental interaction sounds.
- Menu sounds.

Use lightweight synthesized audio or small assets.

Include separate music and sound effect volume controls.

==================================================
15. GRAPHICS SETTINGS
==================================================

Include a functional settings menu.

Graphics options:
- Low.
- Medium.
- High.

Allow adjustment of:
- Particle effects.
- Environmental effects.
- Shadows or lighting effects.
- Screen shake.
- Camera zoom.

Include an FPS-friendly mode.

Settings must actually affect rendering and performance.

==================================================
16. SAVE SYSTEM
==================================================

Implement automatic local saving.

Save:
- Character level.
- Experience.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Unlocked abilities.
- Quest progress.
- Discovered regions.
- Collected items.
- Settings.

Use localStorage or IndexedDB.

The game must preserve progress after refreshing the browser.

==================================================
17. TECHNICAL AND PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

This game must remain lightweight.

Prefer Phaser 3 or a suitable 2D Canvas rendering framework.

Requirements:
- Genuine 2D rendering.
- No unnecessary 3D rendering.
- Efficient tilemap rendering.
- Reusable sprites and animations.
- Texture atlases where useful.
- Object pooling for particles.
- Efficient enemy updates.
- Limited simultaneous effects.
- Responsive rendering.
- Mobile browser support.
- Desktop browser support.
- No mandatory external API.
- No paid API dependencies.

Avoid excessively large assets.

Generate procedural effects when appropriate.

Optimize for mid-range Android phones.

==================================================
18. DEVELOPMENT STRATEGY
==================================================

Build the game in stages.

STAGE 1:
Create the main character, detailed environment, movement, camera and mobile controls.

STAGE 2:
Implement real-time combat, abilities, enemies and health.

STAGE 3:
Create the first explorable region, loot, inventory and basic progression.

STAGE 4:
Add quests, NPCs, world map and additional areas.

STAGE 5:
Implement bosses, skill tree, equipment and advanced progression.

STAGE 6:
Polish graphics, animations, sound and settings.

After each stage, test existing functionality.

Do not attempt to generate an enormous unfinished world in one step.

Prioritize a small but complete playable experience before expanding.

==================================================
19. FINAL QUALITY EXPECTATIONS
==================================================

The finished game should feel like a genuine indie action RPG.

It must have:
- Beautiful detailed pixel art.
- A relatively wide camera view.
- Responsive real-time combat.
- Smooth animations.
- Interesting enemies.
- Meaningful progression.
- Rewarding exploration.
- A functional inventory.
- A satisfying RPG gameplay loop.
- Excellent mobile controls.

Do not create fake buttons or decorative systems that do nothing.

Do not claim features are implemented unless they actually work.

The first playable build should contain one complete region, several enemies, one boss, collectible items, a working progression system and a save system.

Make the game fun to play before expanding its world.

The final result should be visually impressive, lightweight, atmospheric and genuinely enjoyable.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

export function projectType(root) {

    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')

import { startForCapture } from './capture-start.mjs'
import captures from './wip-screenshots.cjs'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

## Objective
- Build a complete, polished, playable 2D open-world action RPG called "ECHOES OF THE FALLEN" as an HTML5 Canvas game in the empty repo at `/home/runner/work/Echo/Echo`.

## Requirements
- 2D pixel art inspired by Hyper Light Drifter/CrossCode/Eastward; wide top-down camera with adjustable zoom (normal/wide/close).
- Five regions: Greenfall Forest, Forgotten Kingdom, Frostbound Mountains, Sunken Depths, Central Sanctuary; interconnected.
- Real-time combat: light/heavy combos, dodge (i-frames), block, 5 abilities (Arcane Burst, Blink, Nova, Frost Bind, Echo Strike), energy/stamina, varied enemies and 3+ bosses with phases/telegraphs.
- RPG progression: level/XP, three skill-tree branches (Arcane, Mobility, Guardian), loot rarities, 24-slot inventory, equipment, shops/upgrades, quests + journal, minimap/world map, secrets/chests/lore, save via localStorage.
- Desktop + mobile touch controls, responsive UI, settings (quality/particles/lighting/screen shake/zoom/audio), synthesized audio.
- Must actually work; no fake systems. No external/paid APIs; lightweight Canvas 2D; no build step required (static server detects `index.html`).
- Final build should include one complete region minimum, enemies, boss, loot, progression, save. Screenshots: small JPEGs, viewport ≤1280px, read only newest.

## Decisions
- Custom Canvas 2D engine (no Phaser/CDN), ES modules, purely procedural pixel art/audio (no external assets).
- Static site: `index.html` at repo root; start script auto-detects `html` type.
- Tile size 16 world px; camera zoom via target visible world height (~370 normal, 460 wide, 290 close; mobile adjusted).
- Five separate region maps (not one seamless map) linked by portals through the Sanctuary hub, plus return portals; Sunken Depths entered via the Sanctuary well after 3 monuments are awakened.
- Rendering uses pre-rendered terrain chunks (16×16 tiles), sorted props/entities, lighting canvas, particle/weather systems, procedural sprites cached in canvases.
- Player sprite drawn procedurally in 3 dirs × states (idle/walk/run/attack/cast/dodge/block/hurt), 6 outfits/4 accessories.
- Main story: Maelin sends player to awaken Root/Crown/Peak monuments (boss-gated), then open the well, descend into Depths, defeat Deep Chorus, touch altar ending. Side quests: locket, wolves, tome, crystals.
- Items/abilities/skills/enemies/bosses defined data-driven in `items.js`; ownership of quests/dialogue in `story.js`.
- Started writing `src/game.js` (Game class) but the write call failed due to payload size; no `game.js` exists yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- Repo inspected (empty except README/Agents/tooling).
- `index.html` created: canvas, HUD skeleton, minimap, objective, vitals, abilities, boss bar, toasts, interact prompt, dialogue box, overlay container, title screen, loading screen, rotate hint, touch controls.
- `style.css` created: full fantasy UI styling incl. title, HUD, panels, inventory, char/skills/quests/map/settings, dialogue, touch controls, responsive breakpoints.
- `src/art.js` created: canvas helpers, RNG/noise, procedural terrain tiles (grass/dirt/path/stone/brick/water/snow/ice/cave/crystal/pave/wood/rock/snowrock/cavewall/moss/snowpath), water shimmer, edge fringe, ~40 props (trees/ancient/pine/snowpine/dead, bushes, rocks, crystals, mushrooms, ferns, pillars, walls, fences, lamps, braziers, chests, graves, statues, banners, bones, shrine, monuments, signposts, flowers), building generator (cottage/ruin/tavern/tower/library/sanctuary/forge/frost/merchant), fountain/well/platform/portrait/tint helpers. Syntax bugs already fixed (`sanctuary` arrow default, pine/snowpine branch, `getNova` stray label).
- `src/sprites.js` created: player frame factory (outfits/accessories/directions/states), NPC sprite generator + portraits for 11 NPCs, enemy sprites (thornling/wolf/knight/wisp/crawler/revenant + bosses grove/hollowking/chorus), FX (slash/orbs/nova/explosion/spark/heal/rune circle/wind/boss slash), item icons + ability icons, enemy dims, shadow sprites.
- `src/world.js` created: tile enum/palettes, 5 map builders with handcrafted landmarks/NPC/chest/lore/portal/enemy/boss/arena data, prop scattering/occupancy, collision queries, map cache, REGIONS metadata.
- `src/items.js` created: rarity table, weapon/armor/charm bases, loot generation + affixes, consumables/materials/cosmetics, inventory helpers absent (to implement), ability definitions, 3-branch skill tree (12 nodes), enemy/boss stat definitions, base stats, XP curve, shop stock, pricing/stat-line helpers.
- `src/story.js` created: 5 quests (main + 4 side) with step markers/done conditions/rewards; dialogue trees for maelin/brann/sera/ilse/pip/garrick/mira/rook/vela/ysra/orin.
- `src/audio.js` created: WebAudio engine with procedural per-region music, ambient beds, boss drums, many SFX, volume/mute controls.

### Active
- Writing the core game logic (`src/game.js`): Game class, input, player movement/combat, enemies/boss AI, projectiles, particles, effects, loot drops, interactions, quests/save/load, map transitions.
- Before that: renderer (`src/render.js`), UI controller (`src/ui.js`), boot/loop (`src/main.js`) still to build. `index.html` references only `src/main.js`, which does not exist yet.

### Blocked
- The attempted `game.js` write was too large and rejected by the tool output limit; must split into smaller files/writes (suggested: `entities.js` + `game.js`, or write game.js in several sequential `edit`/append steps).

## Next Move
1. Create `src/game.js` in smaller chunks (e.g., core class/setup/input first, then player/combat, then enemy/boss AI, then interactions/quests/save). Keep consistent API for renderer/UI: `game.map`, `game.player`, `game.enemies`, `game.projectiles`, `game.particles`, `game.effects`, `game.drops`, `game.camera`, `game.state`, `game.flags`, `game.quests`, `game.settings`, `game.ui`, `game.renderer`.
2. Create `src/render.js`: chunk cache, layered world render (terrain, water shimmer, sorted props/buildings/NPCs/enemies/player/interactables), lighting/darkness + light sources, weather/particles, telegraphs, damage numbers, boss fog wall, camera smoothing/shake, minimap + compass/quest arrow.
3. Create `src/ui.js`: HUD updates, toast, dialogue with typewriter, lore, inventory/equipment, character/outfits, skill tree, quest journal, world map canvas, shop/forge, settings, pause, death, ending, mobile touch wiring.
4. Create `src/main.js`: boot, loading progress, title background (sanctuary vista), loop, resize/DPR, new game/continue, keyboard/mouse listeners, bind renderer/ui.
5. Run static server (e.g. `python3 -m http.server 3002` in tmux) and test with `playwright-cli`; fix JS/console errors, verify combat, quest flow, saving, mobile layout; capture small JPEG screenshots (≤1280px) and inspect latest only.
6. Validate full gameplay loop (new game → Maelin quest → forest boss → 3 monuments → depths → final boss → ending), inventory/save persistence, and settings effects; polish visuals/audio.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/Echo/Echo/index.html`: DOM skeleton, script entry `src/main.js`; must match UI IDs.
- `/home/runner/work/Echo/Echo/style.css`: all UI styling/IDs; touch/mobile rules.
- `/home/runner/work/Echo/Echo/src/art.js`: tiles/props/buildings/fountain/well/portrait/tint exports (`PROPS`, `BUILDINGS`, `getTile`, `getFountain`, `getWell`, `makePortrait`, `tintCanvas`).
- `/home/runner/work/Echo/Echo/src/sprites.js`: player/NPC/enemy/boss/effect/item/ability icon factories, `OUTFITS`, `ACCESSORIES`, `ENEMY_DIMS`, `getPlayerFrame`, `getNPC`, `getPortrait`, `getEnemySprite`, `getSlash`, `getOrbs`, `getNova`, etc.
- `/home/runner/work/Echo/Echo/src/world.js`: `getMap`, `REGIONS`, `TILE`, `T`, `collidesStatic`, `isWaterAt`, `regionInfo`, map/boss/NPC/interactable/portal data.
- `/home/runner/work/Echo/Echo/src/items.js`: items/loot/abilities/skills/enemy stats/boss stats/XP/shop data; missing inventory utility functions.
- `/home/runner/work/Echo/Echo/src/story.js`: `QUESTS`, `NPCS` dialogue nodes and action strings (`startQuest`, `completeQuest`, `shop`, `forge`, `close`, `action: openDepths`, `node`).
- `/home/runner/work/Echo/Echo/src/audio.js`: singleton `audio` (init/setTrack/sfx/setVolumes).
- `/home/runner/work/Echo/Echo/Agents.md`: Linux browser capture workflow guidance.

## Important Context
- `src/main.js` does not exist; page currently fails to load the game.
- No `package.json`; static HTML deployment is required. `start.sh` runs runtime default-start which requires root `index.html`.
- Game loop design: title mode renders sanctuary vista with HUD hidden; new game starts in Sanctuary spawn (34,46 tiles); autosave localStorage key planned as `eotf_save_v1`; save explored grids base64-encoded.
- Map IDs/levels: `sanctuary`(1, 68×58), `greenfall`(2, 140×104), `kingdom`(5, 140×104), `frost`(7, 120×96), `depths`(9, 120×100). Region portals: Sanctuary south↔Greenfall, north↔Kingdom, east↔Frost; Depths via well interactable (`depthWell`) requiring `flags.depthsOpen`.
- Boss keys/flags: `boss:grove` (Greenfall arena at 108,25), `boss:hollowking` (Kingdom 68,29), `boss:frostwarden` (Frost 92,20 elite revenant), `boss:chorus` (Depths 60,84). Arena data stored in `map.arena`.
- Monuments: interactables `monument:greenfall`, `monument:kingdom`, `monument:frost`; Frost requires braziers `brazier:fr_b1..b3` to open `runeGate:fr_gate`; Depths runes `rune:dp_r1..r3` open `runeGate:dp_gate`; altar `dp_altar` triggers ending.
- NPC keys/positions: maelin(34,20), brann(18,31), sera(50,31), ilse(52,47), pip(38,36), garrick(34,51), mira(63,79), rook(49,80), vela(90,60), ysra(33,51), orin(17,65).
- Side quest flags: `locketFound`, `tomeFound`; wolves quest kill progress tracked separately; crystals quest uses `player.resources.crystals >= 8`.
- Player design targets: base 100 HP/energy/stamina, speed ~150 px/s, light combo 3 hits, heavy cost ~20 stamina, dodge ~30 stamina/0.24s i-frames, abilities costs 12/16/28/24/44 with cooldowns 0.7/3.2/6.5/8/13 and unlock levels 1/2/4/6/8.
- Inventory size 24; equipment slots weapon/armor/charm; resources gold/crystals/shards; loot rarities common/uncommon/rare/epic/legendary.
- Buildings' sprites anchor bottom-center; props sort by base Y; sprites have anchors in `ENEMY_DIMS` (`ox`,`oy`) and player frame anchor ≈ (22,41) in 44×46 canvas; NPC sprite 48×50 anchor (24,45).
- `HUD` DOM IDs (from index.html): `hud`, `minimap`, `regionLabel`, `objective`, `objQuest`, `objText`, `levelNum`, `hpFill/hpTxt`, `enFill/enTxt`, `stFill`, `xpFill`, `abilities`, `bossbar/bossName/bossFill/bossPhase`, `toasts`, `interactPrompt/interactText`, `dialogueWrap/dlgName/dlgText/dlgChoices/dlgPortrait`, `overlayWrap/overlay`, `regionBanner/regionName/regionSub`, `titleScreen`, `loading`, `fade`, `hurtFlash`, touch elements (`stickZone`, `stickBase`, `stickKnob`, `touchButtons`, `touchTop`).
- Mobile controls expected: joystick + attack/dodge/interact + ability buttons 1–4, top mini buttons inventory/map/pause; `style.css` has `.tbtn[data-act]` hooks.
- Test tooling: `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`, screenshot to `screenshots/linux.jpg` (small viewport). Use tmux for long-lived server per `Agents.md`.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

content.text:
Now we have a big job: game.js, render.js, ui.js, main.js. Need robust, working game. We need to be efficient but thorough. Let's think architecture.

Files:
- `src/entities.js` maybe helper classes? We can put Player, Enemy, Boss, Projectile, Particle into game.js but split writes.
- `game.js`: imports world/sprites/items/story/audio/art. Contains Game class with update loop, input, combat, AI, interactions, save. Might be 2000 lines. Split: `entities.js` (Player, Enemy, Projectile, Drop, Particle, Effect), `game.js` (Game orchestration, input, interactions, quests, save, combat resolution).
- `render.js`: Renderer class.
- `ui.js`: UI class.
- `main.js`: boot.

Need consistency: game.renderer = new Renderer(canvas, game), game.ui = new UI(game). Circular imports: game.js imports Renderer, UI, but UI imports items etc not game. Renderer imports game? Better pass game instance, no import. main.js imports Game and creates, Game constructor creates Renderer(this) and UI(this) — circular only if render/ui import game class; they won't.

Define key APIs.

World map objects: each map has tiles, solid, props, buildings, npcs, interactables, enemies templates, portals, arena (single arena per map), lore.

Need dynamic state per map instance: visited (map.discovered), explored grid. Interactables dynamic states: chest opened, crystal collected, lore read, monument active, brazier lit, rune lit, gates open, locket/tome found. We'll store `game.flags` with keys `chest:id`, `crystal:id`, `lore:id`, `read:id`, `npc` etc, and flag keys per quest already match (`monument:greenfall`, `brazier:fr_b1`, `rune:dp_r1`). For gates use require arrays. Interactables will be drawn by renderer based on state.

Enemy spawning: maps have `m.enemies` templates. Game keeps `game.spawnedMaps` per map? Approach: when entering map, build enemy entities from templates except defeated flags (boss flag, maybe generic defeated enemies respawn on re-enter — typical). Let's implement each map's enemies spawn on first enter, persist in `game.mapEnemies[id]` arrays of Enemy instances; remove dead; respawn on re-entry? To keep performance and save simplicity, spawn templates anew each time except boss killed flag. But if leave mid-fight enemies reset, fine. Killed ordinary enemies on map get removed; if map reloaded later, respawn. Acceptable. For boss: if `flags['boss:grove']`, don't spawn boss, and arena cleared; boss remains defeated. ## Objective
- Build a complete, polished, playable 2D open-world action RPG “ECHOES OF THE FALLEN” as an HTML5 Canvas game in `/home/runner/work/Echo/Echo`.

## Requirements
- 2D pixel art inspired by Hyper Light Drifter/CrossCode/Eastward; wide top-down camera with adjustable zoom (normal/wide/close).
- Five interconnected regions: Greenfall Forest, Forgotten Kingdom, Frostbound Mountains, Sunken Depths, Central Sanctuary.
- Real-time combat: light/heavy combos, dodge (i-frames), block, 5 abilities (Arcane Burst, Blink, Nova, Frost Bind, Echo Strike), energy/stamina, varied enemies and 3+ bosses with phases/telegraphs.
- RPG progression: level/XP, three skill-tree branches (Arcane, Mobility, Guardian), loot rarities, 24-slot inventory, equipment, shops/upgrades, quests + journal, minimap/world map, secrets/chests/lore, save via localStorage.
- Desktop + mobile touch controls, responsive UI, settings (quality/particles/lighting/screen shake/zoom/audio), synthesized audio.
- Must actually work; no fake systems. No external/paid APIs; lightweight Canvas 2D; no build step (static server detects `index.html`).
- Final build must include one complete region minimum, enemies, boss, loot, progression, save. Screenshots must be small JPEGs, viewport ≤1280px, inspect newest only.

## Decisions
- Custom Canvas 2D engine (no Phaser/CDN), ES modules, procedural pixel art/audio with no external assets.
- Static site: root `index.html`; start script auto-detects HTML.
- Tile size 16 world px; camera zoom via target visible world height (~370 normal, 480 wide, 285 close; mobile ×0.84).
- Five separate region maps linked via Sanctuary portals, plus return portals; Sunken Depths entered via Sanctuary well after 3 monuments awakened.
- Rendering uses full-map pre-rendered terrain canvas, sorted props/entities, lighting canvas, particles/weather, procedural sprites.
- Player sprite drawn procedurally in 3 dirs × states with 6 outfits/4 accessories.
- Main story: Maelin sends player to awaken Root/Crown/Peak monuments (boss-gated), open the well, defeat Deep Chorus, touch altar ending. Side quests: locket, wolves, tome, crystals.
- Data-driven items/abilities/skills/enemies/bosses in `items.js`; quests/dialogue in `story.js`.
- Game architecture split across `entities.js` (Player/Enemy/Projectile/Drop), `game.js` (orchestration/combat/quests/save), `render.js`, `ui.js`, `main.js`.

### Completed

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.

## Objective
- Build and verify a complete, polished, playable 2D open-world action RPG “ECHOES OF THE FALLEN” as an HTML5 Canvas game in `/home/runner/work/Echo/Echo`.

## Requirements
- 2D pixel art inspired by Hyper Light Drifter/CrossCode/Eastward; wide top-down camera with adjustable zoom (normal/wide/close).

"# ECHOES OF THE FALLEN
## A Detailed 2D Open-World Action RPG

Create a complete, highly polished, fully playable 2D action RPG titled \"ECHOES OF THE FALLEN\".

This must be a genuine 2D action RPG with detailed pixel art, real-time combat, exploration, character progression, quests, loot and a large interconnected world.

IMPORTANT: The game must prioritize gameplay depth, beautiful environments, smooth controls and satisfying combat.

Do NOT create a simple platformer, turn-based RPG, idle game or basic top-down walking simulator.

==================================================
1. GAME CONCEPT AND STORY
==================================================

The game takes place in a mysterious fantasy world called AETHERIA.

Long ago, the world was protected by ancient magical structures known as the Echo Monuments.

After a mysterious catastrophe, these structures became corrupted and strange creatures began appearing throughout the world.

Ancient settlements disappeared, forests became dangerous and forgotten civilizations were buried beneath the ruins.

The player controls a young wanderer who discovers an unusual connection to the ancient Echo Monuments.

Explore the world, discover forgotten civilizations, meet interesting characters, uncover hidden locations and gradually discover the truth behind the catastrophe.

Tell the story through exploration, dialogue, environmental storytelling and optional discoveries.

Avoid excessive cinematic cutscenes.

==================================================
2. ART STYLE AND GRAPHICS
==================================================

Create exceptionally detailed 2D pixel art.

Visual inspiration:
- Hyper Light Drifter.
- CrossCode.
- Eastward.
- Modern high-quality pixel-art RPGs.

The game must have:
- Detailed environmental tiles.
- Beautiful character sprites.
- Smooth character animations.
- Animated vegetation.
- Water reflections and movement.
- Atmospheric lighting.
- Animated environmental particles.
- Beautiful spell effects.
- Detailed buildings and architecture.
- Distinctive enemy designs.

Use carefully designed pixel-art palettes.

Avoid generic flat-colored environments.

Make every region visually recognizable.

The world should feel handcrafted rather than randomly assembled.

==================================================
3. CAMERA AND WORLD VIEW
==================================================

Use a top-down camera with a slightly elevated perspective.

IMPORTANT:
The camera must show a relatively LARGE area around the player.

Use a wider camera view than typical zoomed-in RPG games.

The player should remain clearly visible while the camera shows surrounding terrain, enemies, paths and environmental details.

Implement smooth camera following.

Allow adjustable camera zoom in the settings.

Provide:
- Normal zoom.
- Wide zoom.
- Close zoom.

Default to a relatively wide view.

Do not make the world feel cramped.

==================================================
4. WORLD DESIGN
==================================================

Create a large interconnected fantasy world divided into distinct regions.

Initially implement these areas:

A. GREENFALL FOREST
- Dense forests.
- Ancient trees.
- Hidden paths.
- Small settlements.
- Abandoned shrines.
- Forest creatures.

B. THE FORGOTTEN KINGDOM
- Ruined castles.
- Old streets.
- Abandoned buildings.
- Ancient libraries.
- Hidden treasure rooms.

C. FROSTBOUND MOUNTAINS
- Snow-covered terrain.
- Frozen caves.
- Mountain paths.
- Ancient monuments.

D. THE SUNKEN DEPTHS
- Underground caverns.
- Glowing crystals.
- Ancient underground structures.
- Dangerous creatures.

E. THE CENTRAL SANCTUARY
- A peaceful settlement.
- Merchants.
- NPCs.
- Upgrade stations.
- Quest givers.
- A central hub for the player.

Make regions interconnected through paths, caves, gates and shortcuts.

Some locations should require progression or special abilities to access.

Use a consistent world map.

==================================================
5. PLAYER CHARACTER
==================================================

Create a detailed animated pixel-art protagonist.

The player should have:
- Idle animation.
- Walking animation.
- Running animation.
- Dodge animation.
- Attack animation.
- Casting animation.
- Damage animation.

Allow the player to customize:
- Outfit colors.
- Cosmetic accessories.
- Appearance details.

Make the protagonist visually recognizable.

==================================================
6. REAL-TIME COMBAT
==================================================

Combat is one of the most important aspects of this game.

It must feel responsive, fluid and satisfying.

Implement:
- Fast basic attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Combos.
- Dodging.
- Blocking or defensive abilities.
- Magical abilities.
- Area-of-effect attacks.
- Cooldowns.
- Stamina or energy management.

Create several distinct magical abilities:

1. ARCANE BURST
A fast magical projectile.

2. BLINK
A short-distance movement ability that avoids incoming attacks.

3. NOVA
An area attack surrounding the player.

4. FROST BIND
Temporarily slows nearby enemies.

5. ECHO STRIKE
A powerful ability that releases stored magical energy.

Allow abilities to be unlocked and upgraded.

Make combat skill-based rather than button-mashing.

Use clear visual feedback for hits, dodges, enemy attacks and ability activation.

==================================================
7. ENEMIES AND BOSSES
==================================================

Create diverse enemy types.

Examples:
- Small forest creatures.
- Fast aggressive enemies.
- Armored guardians.
- Ranged magical creatures.
- Large elite monsters.
- Ancient corrupted guardians.

Each enemy should have distinct behavior.

Implement:
- Patrol.
- Detection.
- Chasing.
- Attacking.
- Dodging or repositioning.
- Taking damage.
- Defeat animations.

Create several boss encounters.

Bosses should have:
- Unique visual designs.
- Multiple attack patterns.
- Different combat phases.
- Clearly telegraphed attacks.
- Distinctive arenas.
- Rewarding victory sequences.

Boss fights should require learning attack patterns.

==================================================
8. RPG PROGRESSION
==================================================

Create a meaningful character progression system.

Include:
- Character level.
- Experience points.
- Health.
- Energy.
- Stamina.
- Attack power.
- Defense.
- Movement speed.

Enemies and quests reward experience.

Leveling up grants progression points.

Create a skill tree with three branches:

ARCANE:
Focus on magical damage and elemental abilities.

MOBILITY:
Focus on movement, dodging and speed.

GUARDIAN:
Focus on defense, survivability and counterattacks.

Allow players to choose their preferred playstyle.

==================================================
9. LOOT AND EQUIPMENT
==================================================

Create a rewarding loot system.

Item rarities:

- Common.
- Uncommon.
- Rare.
- Epic.
- Legendary.

Add collectible:
- Magical crystals.
- Ancient relics.
- Crafting materials.
- Healing supplies.
- Upgrade components.
- Cosmetic items.

Equipment should have meaningful statistics and visual differences.

Allow the player to inspect, compare and equip discovered items.

Add an inventory with limited space.

Include equipment management and item sorting.

==================================================
10. QUESTS AND NPCS
==================================================

Create a variety of quests.

Main quests:
- Discover ancient monuments.
- Investigate corrupted regions.
- Find missing explorers.
- Recover forgotten artifacts.

Side quests:
- Help villagers.
- Find lost objects.
- Explore hidden locations.
- Defeat dangerous creatures.
- Discover secret areas.

NPCs should have individual dialogue and useful information.

Create a simple quest journal.

Clearly display current objectives.

Avoid repetitive fetch quests as the only form of content.

==================================================
11. EXPLORATION AND SECRETS
==================================================

"# ECHOES OF THE FALLEN
## A Detailed 2D Open-World Action RPG

Create a complete, highly polished, fully playable 2D action RPG titled \"ECHOES OF THE FALLEN\".

This must be a genuine 2D action RPG with detailed pixel art, real-time combat, exploration, character progression, quests, loot and a large interconnected world.

IMPORTANT: The game must prioritize gameplay depth, beautiful environments, smooth controls and satisfying combat.

Do NOT create a simple platformer, turn-based RPG, idle game or basic top-down walking simulator.

==================================================
1. GAME CONCEPT AND STORY
==================================================

The game takes place in a mysterious fantasy world called AETHERIA.

Long ago, the world was protected by ancient magical structures known as the Echo Monuments.

After a mysterious catastrophe, these structures became corrupted and strange creatures began appearing throughout the world.

Ancient settlements disappeared, forests became dangerous and forgotten civilizations were buried beneath the ruins.

The player controls a young wanderer who discovers an unusual connection to the ancient Echo Monuments.

Explore the world, discover forgotten civilizations, meet interesting characters, uncover hidden locations and gradually discover the truth behind the catastrophe.

Tell the story through exploration, dialogue, environmental storytelling and optional discoveries.

Avoid excessive cinematic cutscenes.

==================================================
2. ART STYLE AND GRAPHICS
==================================================

Create exceptionally detailed 2D pixel art.

Visual inspiration:
- Hyper Light Drifter.
- CrossCode.
- Eastward.
- Modern high-quality pixel-art RPGs.

The game must have:
- Detailed environmental tiles.
- Beautiful character sprites.
- Smooth character animations.
- Animated vegetation.
- Water reflections and movement.
- Atmospheric lighting.
- Animated environmental particles.
- Beautiful spell effects.
- Detailed buildings and architecture.
- Distinctive enemy designs.

Use carefully designed pixel-art palettes.

Avoid generic flat-colored environments.

Make every region visually recognizable.

The world should feel handcrafted rather than randomly assembled.

==================================================
3. CAMERA AND WORLD VIEW
==================================================

Use a top-down camera with a slightly elevated perspective.

IMPORTANT:
The camera must show a relatively LARGE area around the player.

Use a wider camera view than typical zoomed-in RPG games.

The player should remain clearly visible while the camera shows surrounding terrain, enemies, paths and environmental details.

Implement smooth camera following.

Allow adjustable camera zoom in the settings.

Provide:
- Normal zoom.
- Wide zoom.
- Close zoom.

Default to a relatively wide view.

Do not make the world feel cramped.

==================================================
4. WORLD DESIGN
==================================================

Create a large interconnected fantasy world divided into distinct regions.

Initially implement these areas:

A. GREENFALL FOREST
- Dense forests.
- Ancient trees.
- Hidden paths.
- Small settlements.
- Abandoned shrines.
- Forest creatures.

B. THE FORGOTTEN KINGDOM
- Ruined castles.
- Old streets.
- Abandoned buildings.
- Ancient libraries.
- Hidden treasure rooms.

C. FROSTBOUND MOUNTAINS
- Snow-covered terrain.
- Frozen caves.
- Mountain paths.
- Ancient monuments.

D. THE SUNKEN DEPTHS
- Underground caverns.
- Glowing crystals.
- Ancient underground structures.
- Dangerous creatures.

E. THE CENTRAL SANCTUARY
- A peaceful settlement.
- Merchants.
- NPCs.
- Upgrade stations.
- Quest givers.
- A central hub for the player.

Make regions interconnected through paths, caves, gates and shortcuts.

Some locations should require progression or special abilities to access.

Use a consistent world map.

==================================================
5. PLAYER CHARACTER
==================================================

Create a detailed animated pixel-art protagonist.

The player should have:
- Idle animation.
- Walking animation.
- Running animation.
- Dodge animation.
- Attack animation.
- Casting animation.
- Damage animation.

Allow the player to customize:
- Outfit colors.
- Cosmetic accessories.
- Appearance details.

Make the protagonist visually recognizable.

==================================================
6. REAL-TIME COMBAT
==================================================

Combat is one of the most important aspects of this game.

It must feel responsive, fluid and satisfying.

Implement:
- Fast basic attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Combos.
- Dodging.
- Blocking or defensive abilities.
- Magical abilities.
- Area-of-effect attacks.
- Cooldowns.
- Stamina or energy management.

Create several distinct magical abilities:

1. ARCANE BURST
A fast magical projectile.

2. BLINK
A short-distance movement ability that avoids incoming attacks.

3. NOVA
An area attack surrounding the player.

4. FROST BIND
Temporarily slows nearby enemies.

5. ECHO STRIKE
A powerful ability that releases stored magical energy.

Allow abilities to be unlocked and upgraded.

Make combat skill-based rather than button-mashing.

Use clear visual feedback for hits, dodges, enemy attacks and ability activation.

==================================================
7. ENEMIES AND BOSSES
==================================================

Create diverse enemy types.

Examples:
- Small forest creatures.
- Fast aggressive enemies.
- Armored guardians.
- Ranged magical creatures.
- Large elite monsters.
- Ancient corrupted guardians.

Each enemy should have distinct behavior.

Implement:
- Patrol.
- Detection.
- Chasing.
- Attacking.
- Dodging or repositioning.
- Taking damage.
- Defeat animations.

Create several boss encounters.

Bosses should have:
- Unique visual designs.
- Multiple attack patterns.
- Different combat phases.
- Clearly telegraphed attacks.
- Distinctive arenas.
- Rewarding victory sequences.

Boss fights should require learning attack patterns.

==================================================
8. RPG PROGRESSION
==================================================

Create a meaningful character progression system.

Include:
- Character level.
- Experience points.
- Health.
- Energy.
- Stamina.
- Attack power.
- Defense.
- Movement speed.

Enemies and quests reward experience.

Leveling up grants progression points.

Create a skill tree with three branches:

ARCANE:
Focus on magical damage and elemental abilities.

MOBILITY:
Focus on movement, dodging and speed.

GUARDIAN:
Focus on defense, survivability and counterattacks.

Allow players to choose their preferred playstyle.

==================================================
9. LOOT AND EQUIPMENT
==================================================

Create a rewarding loot system.

Item rarities:

- Common.
- Uncommon.
- Rare.
- Epic.
- Legendary.

Add collectible:
- Magical crystals.
- Ancient relics.
- Crafting materials.
- Healing supplies.
- Upgrade components.
- Cosmetic items.

Equipment should have meaningful statistics and visual differences.

Allow the player to inspect, compare and equip discovered items.

Add an inventory with limited space.

Include equipment management and item sorting.

==================================================
10. QUESTS AND NPCS
==================================================

Create a variety of quests.

Main quests:
- Discover ancient monuments.
- Investigate corrupted regions.
- Find missing explorers.
- Recover forgotten artifacts.

Side quests:
- Help villagers.
- Find lost objects.
- Explore hidden locations.
- Defeat dangerous creatures.
- Discover secret areas.

NPCs should have individual dialogue and useful information.

Create a simple quest journal.

Clearly display current objectives.

Avoid repetitive fetch quests as the only form of content.

==================================================
11. EXPLORATION AND SECRETS
==================================================

Exploration should be rewarding.

Add:
- Hidden caves.
- Secret rooms.
- Treasure chests.
- Optional boss encounters.
- Ancient puzzles.
- Hidden shortcuts.
- Rare collectible objects.
- Environmental storytelling.

Allow the player to discover things naturally without constantly following quest markers.

Create a minimap and a larger world map.

Show discovered and undiscovered areas differently.

==================================================
12. MOBILE AND DESKTOP CONTROLS
==================================================

Desktop:
- WASD or arrow keys: movement.
- Mouse or keyboard: combat abilities.
- Space: dodge.
- E: interaction.
- I: inventory.
- M: map.
- Escape: pause.

Mobile:
- Left virtual joystick.
- Dedicated attack button.
- Dodge button.
- Three or four ability buttons.
- Interaction button.
- Inventory and map buttons.

Make all mobile controls responsive.

Allow adjustable button sizes and positions if practical.

Support landscape mobile orientation.

Do not let the interface obstruct the gameplay.

==================================================
13. USER INTERFACE
==================================================

Create a beautiful fantasy RPG interface.

During gameplay display:
- Health bar.
- Energy bar.
- Experience bar.
- Character level.
- Current objective.
- Ability cooldowns.
- Minimap.

Create separate interfaces for:
- Main menu.
- Inventory.
- Character stats.
- Skill tree.
- Quest journal.
- World map.
- Equipment.
- Settings.

Use a consistent visual design.

Make menus readable and attractive.

==================================================
14. AUDIO AND ATMOSPHERE
==================================================

Include atmospheric music and sound effects if possible.

Examples:
- Forest ambience.
- Wind.
- Water.
- Footsteps.
- Combat sounds.
- Magical effects.
- Enemy sounds.
- Environmental interaction sounds.
- Menu sounds.

Use lightweight synthesized audio or small assets.

Include separate music and sound effect volume controls.

==================================================
15. GRAPHICS SETTINGS
==================================================

Include a functional settings menu.

Graphics options:
- Low.
- Medium.
- High.

Allow adjustment of:
- Particle effects.
- Environmental effects.
- Shadows or lighting effects.
- Screen shake.
- Camera zoom.

Include an FPS-friendly mode.

Settings must actually affect rendering and performance.

==================================================
16. SAVE SYSTEM
==================================================

Implement automatic local saving.

Save:
- Character level.
- Experience.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Unlocked abilities.
- Quest progress.
- Discovered regions.
- Collected items.
- Settings.

Use localStorage or IndexedDB.

The game must preserve progress after refreshing the browser.

==================================================
17. TECHNICAL AND PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

This game must remain lightweight.

Prefer Phaser 3 or a suitable 2D Canvas rendering framework.

Requirements:
- Genuine 2D rendering.
- No unnecessary 3D rendering.
- Efficient tilemap rendering.
- Reusable sprites and animations.
- Texture atlases where useful.
- Object pooling for particles.
- Efficient enemy updates.
- Limited simultaneous effects.
- Responsive rendering.
- Mobile browser support.
- Desktop browser support.
- No mandatory external API.
- No paid API dependencies.

Avoid excessively large assets.

Generate procedural effects when appropriate.

Optimize for mid-range Android phones.

==================================================
18. DEVELOPMENT STRATEGY
==================================================

Build the game in stages.

STAGE 1:
Create the main character, detailed environment, movement, camera and mobile controls.

STAGE 2:
Implement real-time combat, abilities, enemies and health.

STAGE 3:
Create the first explorable region, loot, inventory and basic progression.

STAGE 4:
Add quests, NPCs, world map and additional areas.

STAGE 5:
Implement bosses, skill tree, equipment and advanced progression.

STAGE 6:
Polish graphics, animations, sound and settings.

After each stage, test existing functionality.

Do not attempt to generate an enormous unfinished world in one step.

Prioritize a small but complete playable experience before expanding.

==================================================
19. FINAL QUALITY EXPECTATIONS
==================================================

The finished game should feel like a genuine indie action RPG.

It must have:
- Beautiful detailed pixel art.
- A relatively wide camera view.
- Responsive real-time combat.
- Smooth animations.
- Interesting enemies.
- Meaningful progression.
- Rewarding exploration.
